findings.title: Cost-budget stops reenter missing-output correction without consuming the step cap

evidence.detail: Pre-budget return sets shouldEndTurn=true without hitStepCap or consuming stepsRemaining.
Non-reviewers default to no maximum missing-output retries.
Correction suppresses only hitStepCap stops; it cannot distinguish budget termination.
Correction resets shouldEndTurn=false, causing another pre-budget short circuit.
Existing test explains why step-cap retries must not be resurrected, but covers ordinary provider steps rather than cost stop.
DI probe observed 3 cost-stop messages, 2 correction messages, zero provider calls, and stepsRemaining still 1; only probe-supplied abort ended it.

findings.trigger: Run a prompt-only non-reviewer template with outputSchema, no output, default maxMissingOutputRetries, maxCostCents=0 (or an already exhausted cost cap), and stepsRemaining>0.
findings.consequence: The intended terminal budget stop becomes an unbounded retry cycle with no LLM call and no step consumption. It repeatedly grows/compacts message history and occupies the run until cancellation; a fixed step cap does not bound it.
findings.suggestedFix: Carry a typed terminal reason from runAgentStep through loopAgentSteps and programmatic steps. Treat budget/step/cancellation stops as terminal incomplete outcomes and run schema correction only after model-requested completion; do not merely add another arbitrary retry limit.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Run the provider-free probe setup with one available step, unset output and maxCostCents=0, remove its observation-triggered abort, and assert one budget stop, zero provider calls, bounded messages, a naturally returned incomplete result and no successful terminal marker. Also cover a cap crossed after one real DI provider step and reviewer/non-reviewer variants.

findings.title: Caught handleSteps errors and aborts are journaled and receipted as completed

evidence.detail: Catch sets endTurn=true for all errors, appends an assistant error string and stores output.error.
It returns the normal programmatic result without propagating a failed/cancelled terminal reason.
The caller interprets endTurn as normal shouldEndTurn.
The loop breaks normally on that flag, bypassing failure/abort catch.
Normal exit writes a terminal completed step boundary.
Normal finishAgentRun is status completed.
Without an explicit terminal failure, a non-mutation child defaults to completed.
Supervised successful-loop settlement uses the same runtime receipt derivation.
DI exception probe observed completed finish, terminal completed journal, and completed/ok/errors=[] child receipt; abort probe observed the same successful finish with parent signal aborted.

findings.trigger: A programmatic generator throws, yields an invalid operation, or encounters an execution rejection inside the main runProgrammaticStep catch. A genuine parent abort thrown there follows the same path.
findings.consequence: The error text is visible, but the machine contract says success: journal replay treats the run as cleanly complete and the parent can receive a completed/ok receipt with no errors. A cancellation can likewise be recorded as completed, undermining task continuation and supervision decisions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an explicit programmatic success/failure/cancellation result or rethrow into the loop terminal handler after preserving current state. The loop must finish as failed/cancelled, preserve pending work, avoid a successful terminal journal marker, and make runtime child receipts derive from that authoritative outcome.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Change the diagnostic exception/abort probes to require failed/cancelled finish statuses, no terminal completed boundary, and child receipts with failed/cancelled status and a typed error. Extend to a rejected awaited tool, partial edits before error, and real supervised bridge settlement; keep an ordinary successful generator control case.

domainAssessment.security: Inspected strict handoff validation, template ceilings, read-only plan inheritance, executable-string trust gate, owner-only supervision files/environment, and cancellation cleanup. No concrete exploit is established. Static hidden programmatic authority remains separate from handoff model-visible tools; broker/sandbox enforcement and full RPC attack surface were not audited.
domainAssessment.correctness: 03-F1 and 03-F2 are dynamically confirmed on the real loop with injected dependencies. Current final-review scope/byte checks and strict missing-output receipt classification are substantial correctness strengths.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Generator and signal cleanup, atomic batch job allocation, path-lease ordering, event reconciliation, per-file pass state and ledger resets were inspected. 03-F2 creates incorrect completed journal/state transitions on failures. No broader race claim or full workspace-lane verification is made.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Actionable prevalidation and typed child transport failures are wired. 03-F1 misroutes terminal budget stops into correction; 03-F2 consumes programmatic exceptions before failed/cancelled handling. Real retry backoff and explicit optional deadlines exist; default unbounded child lifetime is intentional.
domainAssessment.performance: Batch clone caching, bounded background concurrency, bounded receipt/ledger mechanisms, progress-delta pinning, parallel foreground settlement and marker reuse were observed. 03-F1 can grow history and keep CPU/context work alive without provider progress. No latency, throughput or memory benchmark was performed.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: Read agent-runtime and agents manifests. Bun 1.3.5 is declared and used for the probes; runtime dependencies include workspace common, ai range, tokenizer ranges and pinned schema bridge library. Lockfile/advisory/pruned-install auditing was not done, so no package vulnerability or isolated-install claim is made.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Existing typed receipt, step-cap output correction, abort and deterministic generator gate tests were read; real-process bridge tests were inspected but not run. The selected budget suite is helper-only, despite its picker label. New /tmp DI probes reproduce the missing budget-stop discriminator and failure-to-completion propagation; normal gateway/provider end-to-end assurance remains separate.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Strict v1 handoffs/receipts and additive optional fields preserve explicit wire shapes. 03-F1 violates the terminal budget control contract and 03-F2 violates completed/failed/cancelled meaning, even while schemas parse. Default Bun POSIX self-exec support is current; stale SDK/docs wording and request-conditioned writer semantics should be aligned with source.

coverageLimits: This is an orchestration vertical slice, not a full-line audit of base2.ts (15396 lines), run-agent-step.ts (3905 lines) or spawn-agent-utils.ts (4566 lines). Exact observed windows are listed; unobserved specialist waves, writer target/command selectors, bypass parsing, output compaction and mutation extraction remain limits.

All picker-selected ranges were inspected. Adjacent implementation and tests were read only to resolve the terminal-state and wiring hypotheses. Search-only test paths are not treated as full test inspection.

No provider request, network call, source fix, destructive action or project gate test execution was performed. Three /tmp DI/stub-only diagnostic tests ran on cached Bun 1.3.5 and passed their defect-observation assertions; this does not validate production happy paths.

The budget probe deliberately supplied cancellation after the third repeated stop to remain bounded. It demonstrates repeatability without step consumption; infinite duration and memory impact are inferred from the unbounded retry condition, not measured.

Native query_index/read_files audit tools were unavailable in this Codex session. The pinned native inventory and saved picker were used with rg and exact line reads; no unavailable tool call is claimed.

Provider adapters, context/memory quality, terminal/OS sandbox enforcement, SDK durable replay engine/workspace lanes, external model reliability, release performance and broad dependency advisories were assigned elsewhere or excluded.

Capability maturity describes implemented current paths, while assurance describes what was actually inspected/executed. Structural receipts do not prove semantic feature completeness or test adequacy.

recommendedPlanWork.work: Define one authoritative terminal-outcome contract for the loop, programmatic steps, journals and child receipts; fix 03-F1 and 03-F2 through it.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Natural budget return is bounded without an injected abort; generator exceptions/aborts cannot publish completed journal/receipt status; pending task state remains resumable.
recommendedPlanWork.rationale: A model needs trustworthy body state to decide whether to continue, retry or delegate. Parsing schemas cannot recover a terminal reason that the runtime discarded.

recommendedPlanWork.work: Promote the /tmp probes into targeted runtime regressions and add a provider-free vertical generator -> tool -> spawn -> parent receipt matrix.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Cover successful generator, thrown/rejected tool, failure after an edit, unset/schema-invalid/truncated output, zero/crossed budget, user abort while awaiting work, foreground/background and supervised settlement.
recommendedPlanWork.rationale: Helper checks and gen.next gate tests are useful but missed the cross-layer terminal-state contract.

recommendedPlanWork.work: Make budget semantics and supervision support machine-readable and consistent with documentation. Decide explicitly whether a configured cost limit is a soft post-step cap or a shared pre-spend reservation.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: The API reports per-step input versus cumulative tokens, per-attempt timeout/restart multiplication and Bun/POSIX versus Node/Windows process support; if hard aggregate limits are offered, concurrent children and restarts share measured reservations.
recommendedPlanWork.rationale: Do not promise run-wide cost/token/isolation properties from limits that currently mean something narrower.

recommendedPlanWork.work: Keep semantic task decisions in the model, while separating current-edit gate credit, remaining declared workflow and authoritative runtime termination in the control plane.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: A green edit gate does not imply every user objective completed; outstanding model-declared work remains visible without converting parent Git/operator duties into source-repair blockers.
recommendedPlanWork.rationale: The existing soft continuation notice is an appropriate autonomy boundary, but runtime status must describe it faithfully.

recommendedPlanWork.work: Reduce orchestration maintenance coupling by extracting pure state transitions and generated adapters without changing first-party behavior. Align writer/routing documentation with current request-conditioned source.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Parity and generation freshness remain checked; the same vertical probes pass across base2 modes and custom programmatic agents; docs stop claiming unconditional writers or exclusion of compiled POSIX self-exec.
recommendedPlanWork.rationale: The current large inline generator and several return/status surfaces made otherwise strong safeguards inconsistent. This is a maintainability recommendation, not a measured performance claim.
